evals.input: @etymology where does the word sarcasm come from?

etymologies.chain: Proto-Indo-European *twerḱ- > Proto-Indo-European *túrḱs//*twérḱs > Proto-Hellenic *súrks//*swə́rks > Ancient Greek σᾰ́ρξ > Ancient Greek σᾰρκᾰ́ζω > Ancient Greek σαρκασμός > Late Latin sarcasmus > English sarcasm
etymologies.prose: From Late Latin sarcasmus, from Ancient Greek σαρκασμός (“a sneer”), from σαρκάζω (“to gnash the teeth (in anger)”), from σάρξ (“flesh”).

evals.input: @etymology what did Old English wæter come from?

etymologies.chain: Proto-Indo-European *wed- > Proto-Indo-European *wódr̥ > Proto-Germanic *watōr > Proto-West Germanic *watar > Old English wæter
etymologies.prose: From Proto-West Germanic *watar, from Proto-Germanic *watōr, from Proto-Indo-European *wédōr, collective of *wódr̥.
